musical.title: SIX The Musical
musical.based_on: The lives of the six wives of Henry VIII
musical.time_period: Historical figures reimagined in contemporary pop concert setting
musical.vocal_style: Contemporary pop spanning multiple genres — dance-pop, R&B, power ballad, hip-hop, electro-pop, girl-group. Each queen has a distinct pop genre identity.
musical.orchestra_size: All-female band called the 'Ladies in Waiting' (4 players) — keys, guitar, bass, drums
musical.synopsis: The six wives of Henry VIII take the stage as a girl-group pop concert, each queen performing a solo number to prove SHE had it worst and therefore deserves to be the lead singer. From Catherine of Aragon's Beyoncé-inspired anthem through to Catherine Parr's reflective finale, the queens compete — until they realise that defining themselves by their suffering at the hands of one man misses the point entirely. Together, they choose to rewrite their stories on their own terms.

roles.name: Catherine of Aragon
roles.description: The first wife — proud, powerful, and FURIOUS. Catherine was a Spanish princess, Queen of England for over 20 years, and refused to accept Henry's annulment. She opens the competition with fierce Beyoncé-inspired energy, demanding recognition for what she endured and never backing down.

vocal.tessitura: Upper belt with gospel/R&B power. Sustained belting throughout.
vocal.style_notes: Beyoncé-inspired power pop with gospel and R&B influences. Must have extraordinary belt power and sustain. 'No Way' is a relentless belt showcase demanding vocal stamina and fierce attitude. Think Beyoncé meets Destiny's Child.

dance.stamina: High — opens the show with maximum energy
dance.notes: Concert-style pop choreography. Must command the stage with queen energy from the first note. Beyoncé-level confidence in movement.

acting.emotional_range: Focused — righteous fury, pride, defiance, eventual solidarity
acting.notes: Catherine sets the competitive tone. She's not just angry — she's REGAL. Must convey the gravity of a 24-year marriage and political betrayal while being a pop star. The audience script interactions require confidence and improvisation ability.

casting_insights.why: Aragon opens the show and must grab the audience immediately with vocal power and stage command. 'No Way' is one of the most demanding belt showcases in modern musical theatre. This role develops power belt technique, concert presence, and fierce confidence.
casting_insights.common_casting: Powerhouse belters with natural authority and R&B/gospel vocal quality. Must own the stage from the first note.
casting_insights.standout_opportunity: 'No Way' is a vocal EVENT — when the belt is right, it sets the standard for the entire show.

skills_developed: Opening a show with maximum impact
challenge_areas: Setting the energy bar for the entire show
Maintaining regal authority in pop concert format
recommended_for: Power belters wanting a showcase role
Performers with R&B/gospel vocal background
Those developing concert-style stage presence

what_directors_look_for: The ability to open a show and set the bar
common_mistakes: All power, no emotional connection
Running out of voice on sustained belts
Not enough regal quality — she's a QUEEN, not just a singer
tips: Catherine was queen for 24 YEARS and refused to give up her crown — play that resolve
Study Beyoncé's stage presence — the confidence, the power, the control
Vocal health is crucial — 'No Way' demands sustained belt that must be sustainable
She's righteous, not bitter — there's an important difference

key_songs.title: No Way
key_songs.notes: Beyoncé-inspired power anthem. Sustained belt showcase. Sets the bar for the entire show.

key_songs.title: Ex-Wives
key_songs.notes: Opening number introducing all six queens. Full company energy.

key_songs.title: Six / Megasix
key_songs.notes: Finale number. Unity anthem with all queens.

roles.name: Anne Boleyn
roles.description: The second wife — witty, irreverent, and refuses to be defined by her beheading. Anne was the most provocative of Henry's wives, and in SIX she channels that energy into a cheeky, darkly funny pop-punk anthem. She turns her own execution into a punchline while making a powerful point about how history has treated her.

vocal.tessitura: Upper belt with pop-punk edge and spoken-word elements
vocal.style_notes: Lily Allen / Avril Lavigne inspired pop-punk with attitude. Cheeky, irreverent vocal delivery that mixes singing with spoken word and comedy timing. Must belt powerfully while maintaining comedic delivery.

dance.notes: Anne's movement is playful, provocative, and slightly chaotic — she's having the most fun of any queen. Physical comedy elements throughout.

acting.emotional_range: Comedy with surprising depth — irreverence, dark humor, genuine anger at injustice, defiance
acting.notes: Anne gets the biggest laughs in the show — her beheading jokes are legendary. But underneath the humor is a woman refusing to be a victim. The comedy must land while the underlying message hits even harder.

casting_insights.why: Anne Boleyn is the audience favourite in most productions — she gets the most laughs and the most memorable moments. 'Don't Lose Ur Head' is a comedy masterpiece that also packs an emotional punch. This role develops comedy-in-concert skills and dark humor delivery.
casting_insights.common_casting: Charismatic, funny performers with strong pop voices and natural comedic timing. The performer who makes the audition room laugh.
casting_insights.standout_opportunity: 'Don't Lose Ur Head' — the beheading puns, the audience interaction, the pop-punk energy — is often the most-quoted number from the show.

challenge_areas: Keeping the comedy fresh every performance
Not letting the laughs overshadow the message
recommended_for: Natural comedians with strong pop voices
Performers who thrive on audience interaction
Those developing comedy-in-music skills
Pop-punk vocalists wanting a theatrical showcase

what_directors_look_for: The ability to be hilarious AND meaningful
common_mistakes: All comedy, no substance — Anne has a point to make
Trying too hard to be funny — the material does the work if you commit
Not enough vocal power beneath the comedy
tips: Anne is the funniest queen but she's also making the most radical point — she RECLAIMS her death
Study Lily Allen's delivery — cheeky, sharp, darkly funny
The beheading jokes only work with total commitment — don't apologise for them
Audience interaction must feel spontaneous even though it's rehearsed

key_songs.title: Don't Lose Ur Head
key_songs.notes: Pop-punk comedy anthem. Dark humor, beheading puns, audience interaction. The most-quoted number.

key_songs.title: Ex-Wives
key_songs.notes: Opening number. Anne's irreverent energy sets the tone.

roles.name: Jane Seymour
roles.description: The third wife — gentle, maternal, and the only one Henry truly mourned. Jane died in childbirth giving Henry his longed-for son. In SIX, she channels Adele-inspired power ballad energy, presenting herself as the ultimate sacrifice. Her number is the emotional gut-punch of the show.

vocal.voice_type: Soprano / Mezzo with power ballad belt
vocal.tessitura: Builds from tender low register to soaring high belt. The widest dynamic range of any queen.
vocal.style_notes: Adele-inspired power ballad. Must start tender and intimate, then build to an overwhelming vocal climax. 'Heart of Stone' requires extraordinary dynamic range — whisper-soft verses exploding into massive belted chorus. This is the vocal showpiece of the entire show.

dance.stamina: Moderate — the vocal demands are the main physical challenge
dance.notes: Jane's number is the most still in the show — standing and delivering vocal emotion rather than dancing. The power comes from the voice, not the movement.

acting.emotional_range: Primarily emotional depth — tenderness, sacrifice, love, quiet strength, devastating vulnerability
acting.notes: Jane is the emotional centre of the show. Her number slows everything down and demands that the audience FEEL. Must convey genuine maternal love and the tragedy of dying for your child. The gentleness makes the vocal power all the more devastating.

casting_insights.why: 'Heart of Stone' is widely considered the vocal highlight of SIX — a power ballad that requires the greatest dynamic range and emotional delivery of any number in the show. This role develops ballad technique, emotional authenticity, and the ability to stop a show with pure vocal power.
casting_insights.common_casting: The strongest pure singer in the company. Must have extraordinary dynamic range — genuine pianissimo to full-power belt. Adele-level vocal quality.
casting_insights.standout_opportunity: 'Heart of Stone' stops the show. When the belt kicks in, the audience physically reacts. This is a career-defining vocal moment.

skills_developed: Power ballad technique and dynamic range
Making an audience feel through pure voice
challenge_areas: The dynamic range demand is extraordinary
Sustaining emotional truth over many performances
The transition from gentle to powerful must feel organic
recommended_for: Exceptional vocalists wanting THE ballad showcase
Performers who communicate emotion through voice
Those developing dynamic range and control
Singers who want to stop the show

what_directors_look_for: Extraordinary vocal range and dynamic control
The ability to start at a whisper and build to a roar
The ability to make a room silent with voice alone
common_mistakes: Starting too loud — the quiet beginning is essential
All technique, no emotion — Jane must FEEL
Rushing the build — let it breathe
Not enough power for the climax
tips: Jane died so her son could live — that's the emotional core of everything
Study Adele's live performances — the build, the control, the emotional devastation
'Heart of Stone' needs to build like a wave — start as a ripple, end as a tsunami
The gentleness makes the power shocking — protect the quiet moments

key_songs.title: Heart of Stone
key_songs.notes: THE power ballad of the show. Whisper to belt. Emotional devastation. Stops the show.

key_songs.title: Ex-Wives
key_songs.notes: Opening number. Jane's gentler energy contrasts with the other queens.

key_songs.title: Six / Megasix
key_songs.notes: Finale. Jane's gentle strength within the unity.

roles.name: Anna of Cleves
roles.description: The fourth wife — the one who WON. Henry annulled their marriage after six months because she wasn't attractive enough (according to him), but Anna negotiated the best divorce settlement in history and lived happily ever after as the richest woman in England. She's the show's celebration queen — confident, savvy, and living her best life.

vocal.voice_type: Mezzo / Alto with hip-hop flow and belt
vocal.tessitura: Lower to mid range with rap/spoken word sections and belt moments
vocal.style_notes: Nicki Minaj / Lizzo inspired hip-hop pop with swagger. Must handle rap verses, spoken word, and belt chorus. 'Get Down' (or 'Haus of Holbein'/'Get Down') is a party anthem requiring vocal versatility and stage command. Attitude and flow over pure vocal power.

dance.notes: Anna's number is the biggest dance party of the show. Must command hip-hop choreography with confidence and swagger. This is the party queen — movement should feel celebratory and powerful.

acting.emotional_range: Primarily celebration and confidence — smugness, joy, independence, triumph
acting.notes: Anna is the queen who refused to be a victim and came out on top. Her energy is pure celebration — she got the money, the houses, and the freedom. Must convey both the party energy and the shrewd intelligence that got her there.

casting_insights.why: Anna is the party of the show — her number lifts the entire audience to their feet. This role develops hip-hop performance, rap delivery, and the ability to turn a theatre into a nightclub. The swagger required is career-building.
casting_insights.common_casting: Versatile performers with hip-hop dance skills, rap ability, and infectious party energy. Must own the room like a headliner.
casting_insights.standout_opportunity: 'Get Down' transforms the theatre into a party. When the energy is right, it's the most fun number in the show.

challenge_areas: Sustaining party energy at concert level
Making the celebration feel genuine, not forced
recommended_for: Performers with hip-hop/rap skills wanting theatrical showcase
Dancers with pop/hip-hop background
Those developing stage command and swagger
Performers who naturally energise a room

what_directors_look_for: The ability to turn any room into a party
common_mistakes: Forcing the party energy rather than letting it flow
Weak rap delivery — the flow must be tight
Not enough dance commitment
Playing Anna as just party without the intelligence underneath
tips: Anna OUTSMARTED Henry VIII — she's not just a party girl, she's the smartest person in the room
Study Nicki Minaj and Lizzo — the confidence, the flow, the ownership
The rap sections need practice — flow and rhythm must be effortless
Your number should make every person in the audience want to dance

key_songs.title: Get Down
key_songs.notes: Hip-hop party anthem. Rap verses, belt chorus, dance breakdown. The party of the show.

key_songs.title: Ex-Wives
key_songs.notes: Opening number. Anna brings the sass.

key_songs.title: Six / Megasix
key_songs.notes: Finale. Anna's party energy in the collective.

roles.name: Katherine Howard
roles.description: The fifth wife — the youngest queen, beheaded at just 19. Katherine's story is the most tragic, dealing with grooming, abuse, and exploitation. In SIX, she initially presents a bubbly pop princess persona before revealing the devastating truth beneath. Her number is the emotional turning point of the entire show.

vocal.tessitura: Bright pop soprano that shifts to raw, emotional belt. The contrast is devastating.
vocal.style_notes: Ariana Grande / Britney Spears inspired bubbly pop that transforms into raw emotional power. 'All You Wanna Do' starts as a sexy pop number and gradually reveals itself as a harrowing account of abuse. The vocal shift from performative pop to genuine pain is the show's most demanding acting-through-singing moment.

dance.notes: Katherine's choreography starts as confident pop princess staging and gradually breaks down as the song reveals its true nature. The physical storytelling of the number's transformation is crucial.

acting.emotional_range: Extreme — performed bubbly confidence, gradually revealing manipulation, abuse, desperation, and raw vulnerability
acting.notes: The most emotionally demanding role in SIX. Katherine's number is essentially a trauma reveal disguised as a pop song. The performer must sell the bubbly exterior convincingly enough that the gradual revelation is devastating. This requires extraordinary emotional control and the ability to break the audience's hearts.

special_skills: Emotional transformation within a single song
Pop princess performance that shifts to raw truth

casting_insights.why: Katherine Howard has the most dramatically complex number in SIX — a song that changes meaning as it unfolds. This role develops the incredibly sophisticated skill of performing one thing while gradually revealing another. The emotional demand is extraordinary and the growth potential is immense.
casting_insights.common_casting: Young pop sopranos with genuine emotional depth and the maturity to handle sensitive content. Must be able to perform bubbly pop convincingly while carrying devastating subtext.
casting_insights.standout_opportunity: 'All You Wanna Do' is the moment the show transforms from entertainment to art. When this number works, the audience is shattered.

skills_developed: Performing subtext — saying one thing while revealing another
Emotional transformation within a single number
Handling sensitive content with maturity and care
Pop vocal technique with dramatic depth
Breaking the fourth wall of performance itself
challenge_areas: The emotional toll of performing trauma every show
Making the bubbly opening convincing enough for the reveal to work
The gradual transformation must be precisely calibrated
recommended_for: Emotionally mature young performers
Pop sopranos with acting depth
Those ready for the most challenging emotional performance in the show
Performers wanting to develop subtext performance skills

what_directors_look_for: The ability to be genuinely bubbly AND devastatingly vulnerable
Emotional maturity to handle the content
The precise calibration of the song's transformation
common_mistakes: Telegraphing the darkness too early — the bubbly opening must be convincing
Not being emotionally ready for the content
Rushing the reveal — it needs to dawn gradually
All emotion, no vocal control — the singing must remain strong
tips: Katherine was 19 when she was killed — hold that youth and vulnerability
The number works because Katherine doesn't realise at first what's happening to her — play the gradual awareness
This role requires emotional self-care — develop rituals for before and after performances
Study how pop music can mask pain — that's the entire mechanism of the number

key_songs.title: All You Wanna Do
key_songs.notes: Pop number that transforms into a harrowing abuse reveal. The most emotionally complex number in the show.

roles.name: Catherine Parr
roles.description: The sixth and final wife — the survivor, scholar, and the one who changes the game. Catherine Parr was the most educated queen, a published author, and she outlived Henry. In SIX, she's the one who stops the competition and challenges the other queens to define themselves beyond their relationship with one man. Her number is the show's thesis statement.

vocal.tessitura: Mid-range that builds to powerful belt. Reflective to triumphant.
vocal.style_notes: Alicia Keys / Emeli Sandé inspired reflective pop that builds to anthemic power. 'I Don't Need Your Love' starts intimate and personal, building to a declaration of independence. The voice should feel wise, warm, and ultimately triumphant.

dance.stamina: Moderate — the vocal and emotional demands are primary
dance.notes: Catherine Parr's number is more about presence than dance. She's the philosopher of the group — her power is in her words and voice, not her movement.

acting.emotional_range: Deep — reflection, wisdom, challenge, vulnerability, hope, triumph
acting.notes: Catherine Parr has the most important dramatic function — she changes the entire direction of the show. She must convincingly challenge five powerful women to reconsider their approach. Her number needs to feel like a genuine revelation, not a lecture. She's the most mature queen emotionally.

special_skills: Changing the direction of a show

casting_insights.why: Catherine Parr delivers the show's thesis — and must do so with enough conviction to redirect an entire evening. This role develops the sophisticated skill of changing an audience's emotional direction, delivering philosophical ideas through pop music, and closing a show with meaning.
casting_insights.common_casting: Emotionally intelligent performers with strong pop-belt voices and natural wisdom. Must feel like the most mature, thoughtful person in the room.
casting_insights.standout_opportunity: 'I Don't Need Your Love' is the moment the show transcends entertainment and becomes a statement. When it works, the audience's understanding of everything they've seen shifts.

skills_developed: Closing a show with meaning and power
challenge_areas: The number must redirect the show without feeling preachy
Following Katherine Howard's devastating number is a huge challenge
recommended_for: Thoughtful performers with genuine emotional intelligence
Pop belters wanting to deliver meaningful content
Those developing the ability to change an audience's emotional direction
Performers who want to close the show with purpose

what_directors_look_for: Emotional intelligence and wisdom beyond years
Strong pop belt that builds organically
The ability to deliver ideas through song convincingly
Natural authority earned through thoughtfulness, not force
The quality of a leader who leads by example
common_mistakes: Being preachy — the message must be felt, not lectured
Not enough vocal power for the anthemic climax
Lacking the gravitas to redirect the show
Playing too young — Catherine Parr needs maturity
tips: Catherine Parr was a published author and scholar — play the intellectual depth
She's not telling the other queens they're wrong — she's offering a better way forward
Study Alicia Keys' performance style — wise, warm, building, powerful
Your number follows Katherine Howard's devastation — you must lift the audience from that place
